subject: Clarify: SOC 2 coverage for Dedicated pools with hosted fallback/burst
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fincocap.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marta.ruiz@fincocap.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 question re: dedicated pools + hosted fallback

Hi Chloe,

Quick question from our security team as we prepare procurement: our architecture would point traffic at your Dedicated GPU pool most of the time, but we understand Redwood supports burst/fallback to the hosted fleet if capacity is exhausted. For the SOC 2 Type II period you're providing evidence for, can you confirm whether requests that are routed to hosted for short bursts would be covered under the same SOC 2 scope/bridge letter? Our auditors want to know: 1) whether logs/evidence include those fallback events, and 2) if a bridge letter is sufficient to cover intermittent routing into hosted.

Also asking whether there's a way to restrict fallback for our tenancy only (policy-level control) — if so that may simplify things for auditors.

Thanks,
Samir
Security Architect, FinCo Capital

Attachment: FinCo_Audit_Qs_090626.xlsx (excel)
From: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fincocap.com>
Cc: marta.ruiz@fincocap.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 question re: dedicated pools + hosted fallback

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear question and the attached spreadsheet (downloaded). Short answer: yes, we can cover burst/fallback events in evidence, but there are nuance and configuration choices that affect which artifacts auditors will see. High level:  

- If your deployment is Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated pool) and we perform the fallback to Redwood-hosted resources under Redwood control, those fallback events are within Redwood's operational environment and can be represented in the SOC 2 Type II evidence (logs, change records, incident records) for the covered period.
- If you run Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem runtime), and the fallback would route outside your private environment into hosted, that path is out-of-scope unless explicitly included in the bridge letter and we can provide compensating evidence.

Two follow-ups so we can be precise for your auditors:
1) Is your Dedicated pool provisioned as a Redwood-managed tenant in our Dedicated offering (we host GPUs but isolate via tenant controls), or is it deployed into a customer-dedicated VPC?
2) Will you accept a bridge letter that describes intermittent hosted fallback and points auditors to token-level routing logs / routing policy config as evidence, or do you require the hosted environment to be fully in-scope (i.e., included in the formal SOC report)?

I asked Karthik (cc'd) to add technical detail about the artifacts we can produce. Will follow up with a short package (summary + sample logs + bridge letter template).

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SOC 2 question re: dedicated pools + hosted fallback

Hi Samir / Chloe — added some specifics here from an infra/ops perspective.

Quick bullet answers:
- Evidence we can provide when Dedicated is Redwood-managed and fallback happens into Redwood-hosted:
  * Router traces showing routing decision (request id, timestamp, source tenant id, destination pool id)
  * Token-level latency logs and per-token accounting for the request in our telemetry store (retained for the audit window)
  * Audit logs for autoscaling/burst events and capacity alarms that caused fallback
  * Sample deployment manifests and routing policy config snapshots for the audit period

- If your Dedicated is deployed into your own VPC (customer-managed), fallback into Redwood-hosted is a cross-boundary event. We can still provide a bridge letter describing the behavior and include exported logs from the Redwood side, but your auditors typically ask for complementary evidence from your side (VPC flow logs, routing ACLs) to accept the bridge.

Policy control options:
- Tenant-level routing policy (recommended): we can enforce a strict "no-fallback" policy for a tenant so requests never leave the Dedicated pool. This is a config change we can implement and document; auditors like this as it constrains the scope.
- Soft-fallback (default for burst): fallback into hosted is enabled to guarantee availability; we log all such events.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which Dedicated deployment model you have (Redwood-managed vs customer VPC).
2) If you want the cleanest audit boundary, request "no-fallback" during the audit window; we can enable and provide a config snapshot + change record.
3) If intermittent fallback is acceptable, we will bundle the routing logs + bridge letter that calls out the caveat and links to the sample artifacts.

I attached a short summary doc and the bridge letter template for review. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the artifacts with your auditors.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 question re: dedicated pools + hosted fallback

Samir — following up with a concrete proposal based on Karthik's notes:

Proposal for the audit window (Sep 1–Oct 31, 2026):
- Option A (preferred for clean scope): We will enable tenant-level "no-fallback" during the audit window so all your traffic remains within your Dedicated pool. Evidence package: policy snapshot, change record, and routing traces showing zero fallback events for the period.

- Option B (if you need burst guarantees): Keep soft-fallback enabled. Evidence package: routing traces for all fallback events, per-request token logs, autoscaling alarm history, and a signed bridge letter that explicitly documents that hosted fallback occurred and points auditors to the Redwood artifacts. We will also request complementary network logs from your side if your Dedicated is deployed into a customer-managed VPC.

If you confirm Option A, we'll schedule a brief maintenance window (non-disruptive config update) and provide the SOC evidence pack at the end of the audit window. If Option B, we'll prepare the bridge letter now (attached) and send a sample of the routing logs for your auditors to review.

Would you like us to proceed with Option A or B? If helpful, I can set up a 30-minute call with Karthik and Laura to run through the artifacts with your auditor rep.

Thanks — Chloe

Redwood Inference
